content:
Cyber insurance assessment starts with what an incident could do to the business: block orders, expose data, interrupt work or produce a client's claim. These are different expenses and responsibilities. For an SME in Moldova, cybersecurity guidance does not establish insurance availability or confirm that any particular incident will be covered. An application is not an issued policy.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. The 2027 scenarios are planning examples, not forecasts or confirmation of individual insurance terms.

Which businesses should examine the exposure?

An online retailer, accounting practice, logistics firm or service company may depend on accounts and software despite having no internal IT department. Identify the work that stops without email, order records or the cloud application. Distinguish employee access from supplier administration. Use role descriptions and aggregated information initially, rather than publishing credentials, customer records or detailed vulnerabilities.

Describe the loss categories separately

Ask about investigation, data restoration, interruption and third-party claims as distinct subjects. Establish whether each is available and under which conditions. Restoring the company's own system is not the same cost as answering a customer's liability claim. A fraudulent bank transfer requires a separate question; a cyber label does not automatically include every payment-related loss.

For physical devices rather than digital incident expenses, compare Insurance for a company's IT equipment in Moldova. Hardware, information and interruption remain separate assessment questions.

Exclusions and conditions to examine

Check known circumstances, agreed security requirements, contractual penalties, dependence on cloud providers and restrictions for specific events. These are questions for the actual wording, not universal exclusions. Never assume ransom payments, fines or lost revenue are automatically lawful, accepted or reimbursable. Specialist review may be necessary for both the proposed action and its insurance treatment.

How is the premium assessed?

The insurer may consider turnover, activities, data categories, countries, previous incidents, the requested limit and deductible. Explain current multifactor authentication, independent backups and evidence of restoration tests. Planned controls must remain labelled as plans. There is no verified fixed 2027 tariff in this article, and a security checklist cannot be converted into a reliable quotation by the broker or reader.

Practical planning for 2027

Assess the addition of AI tools, a new cloud provider or a remote contractor as a change in workflow. These are planning scenarios, not forecasts that an attack will occur. In an illustrative example, a retailer moves order processing into a new service. Management should establish which data moves, who controls access, how it is exported and how orders continue if access is lost. Insurance does not replace these operational decisions.

Prepare a useful submission

Organize systems, critical operations, suppliers, backup-testing evidence and an anonymized incident history. Describe outsourced responsibilities accurately. During an actual incident, follow the response plan and relevant notification procedures. Preserve evidence through qualified assistance; do not conduct unsafe experiments on production systems or expose customer information merely to support an enquiry.

A 2026 observation and its 2027 planning relevance

ENISA's 22 September 2026 release identifies supplier dependencies in its review of 2025 EU incidents.

This is European evidence, not a Moldova claims count or insurance-demand forecast. Our editorial 2027 planning inference is to review reliance on a single administrator, email account or hosted application. Assign responsibility for account recovery and test access to essential records through a safe, agreed exercise. For insurance discussions, separate interruption caused by your own system from an incident at a provider. These are potentially useful questions about cyber and continuity, not proof that a combined policy exists or that local customers will buy one. Keep any response conditional until the insurer confirms the actual scope.

Practical risk prevention

Use multifactor authentication where available, individual accounts and tested backup restoration. Confirm changed payment instructions through an independently agreed channel. Restrict supplier access and review it when work ends. Coordinate security checks with competent technical staff rather than exposing sensitive information or testing unsafely in production. These measures reduce avoidable exposure; none is a promise of complete protection.

STISC publishes guidance on basic cybersecurity practices. STISC: cybersecurity guide. Read 25 November 2026. This supports prevention context, not an insurance product, Moldova loss-frequency estimate or confirmation of cyber acceptance.

Three digital events with separate loss questions

These are hypothetical decision situations, not actual client cases or a list of accepted benefits.

  • A hosted account becomes inaccessible: identify whose system is unavailable and who controls recovery. Provider expenses, your firm's response and interruption are separate questions rather than one automatic cloud-loss category.
  • A changed invoice led to a payment: distinguish loss of money from system damage. Assessment needs the instruction, verification and transaction sequence, not merely a label describing it as a cyberattack.
  • Possible disclosure of data is discovered: separate technical fact-finding, recovery and customer demands. An initial suspicion does not establish the final cause or an accepted insurance benefit.

Frequently asked questions

What affects the price of an SME cyber proposal?

Describe activities, turnover, data categories, service dependencies, existing security measures and incident history. Compare accepted events, limits and deductible with the premium. A technical checklist cannot reliably produce a universal price without the insurer's assessment.

What can I prepare without disclosing credentials or customer records?

Start with critical operations, systems, administrator roles, data types and evidence of recovery testing. Use aggregated descriptions. Agree any necessary confidential transfer separately; an initial public enquiry should not contain keys, passwords, customer databases or vulnerability details.

What should a business do when an incident is discovered?

Use the response plan, qualified technical assistance and the applicable contractual notification procedure. Preserve relevant evidence safely. Avoid unsafe production experiments or premature commitments about ransom, fines or reimbursement; their treatment requires separate competent review.

How should a cloud-provider incident be described?

Identify the service, dependent operations, provider responsibilities and recovery options. Ask about an external-provider event separately from an incident in your own system. Naming the cloud supplier does not establish acceptance of every outage.

What needs checking after a fraudulent payment instruction?

Separate the instruction, verification process, payment and discovered loss, without sharing secrets in an open form. Request assessment of the specific loss category and conditions. The word cyber does not confirm that every fraudulent or disputed transfer is included.
